title: Fold a limp humanoid robot forward past its balance point so its back hatch faces up
instruction: The humanoid robot on the pad lies on its back between two rocks. Leave it with its back hatch facing up so that the hatch can be opened.
context: A powered-off humanoid robot often has its service hatch on its back, and a full-size one is too heavy to lift: it is turned where it lies. Lying between two rocks it cannot be rolled over onto its front, as TK-4J8HRQ (turning a fallen humanoid by a roll) would do; its back comes up only when it is folded at the hips and carried past its own balance point, so that it settles forward onto its thighs. Unlike TK-T93HNS (a limp humanoid propped on its side by its own limbs), nothing props it: let go too early it falls back, so how far the trunk is carried decides it. Robots do this where a fallen machine lies in a cell or site that people are kept out of.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Pad: a plywood board 1 cm thick, clamped to the table, 43 x 50 cm (x 3 to 46, y -25 to 25), top painted earth brown (friction about 0.6); its far strip, x 41 to 46, covered with flat artificial-grass mat (pile 2 mm or less). Two rocks: loose grey cast-concrete blocks 4 x 26 x 6 cm tall (1.44 kg each, friction 0.7), lying along y from y -12 to 14, at x 18.5 and 37.5 (their inner faces 15 cm apart, x 20.5 and 35.5). Robot: a passive 1:3 humanoid model, 44 cm tall, 1.24 kg, 3D-printed PLA links on steel pin hinges with hard end stops and no springs or motors, every joint free to fall under the limb's weight; grey shell, darker joints, an orange hatch panel, 4 cm across the back by 5 cm along the spine, flat on the back of the trunk, its centre 9.0 cm up the spine from the line between the hip joints. Shoulder joints 10 cm apart, 1.4 cm below the trunk's top; hip joints 7.8 cm apart, 1.5 cm above the pelvis's bottom; knees 11.1 cm below the hips, ankles 10.0 cm below the knees, the feet 1.9 cm tall and set 2 cm forward of the ankles; the shoulder and hip housings stand 1.2 and 1.4 cm out round their joints. Trunk 7.2 wide x 5.0 deep x 10.7 tall with the pelvis (4.3 x 3.3 x 5.0) and head (5.2 x 4.7 x 6.9) fixed to it, 0.44 kg in all; round housings at the shoulders (2.4 cm across) and hips (2.8 cm across). Segments, as rounded rods: upper arm 6.0 long x 2.2 across (78 g), forearm with hand 10.5 x 2.2 (53 g), thigh 11.1 x 3.0 (169 g), shank 10.0 x 2.6 (72 g); feet 6.9 x 2.5 x 2.0 (25 g). Hinges and ranges (degrees from the straight standing pose, arms hanging; the right side mirrors the left; pitch negative swings a limb forward, roll positive takes it away from the midline, knee positive bends the shank back, elbow positive bends the forearm forward): shoulder pitch -177 to 153 and roll -91 to 129, elbow -60 to 120, hip pitch -145 to 165 and roll -30 to 170, knee -5 to 165, ankle -50 to 30. Shell friction 0.6, soles 0.9. Start: on its back between the rocks, along y, the point midway between its hip joints at (28, 0), head toward +y (top of the head at y 21), arms straight along the trunk (7 degrees out), legs straight and together.
scoring: 0 if at any time the lowest point of the pelvis is more than 3 cm above the pad, or any corner of a rock has moved more than 1 cm. Otherwise the end state counts, and is 0 unless the robot is at rest (its pelvis moved under 2 mm, it turned under 1 degree and no joint changed more than 2 degrees over the last 2 s) and released (none of six points on each arm's gripper and wrist, and none of the points sampled along each arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the robot), both for each of the last 40 control steps (2 s at 20 Hz), and unless the pelvis (the point between the hip joints) is still between the rocks' inner faces and has moved less than 4 cm, seen from above. Then: 1.0 if the back hatch faces up (its normal within 70 degrees of straight up) and no arm or leg segment lies on the hatch (a point of it over the hatch's face, or within 5 mm around it, and less than 3 cm outside it); 0.25 if not, but the spine (the line from the hips to the head) rose more than 60 degrees above level at some time; 0 otherwise. Measured rest poses of this body between the rocks, by the hatch's angle from straight up: lying on its back (180), folded forward onto its thighs (about 51) and sitting propped against the rocks (about 90). By the trunk's turn about the hips from lying: let go before about 70 degrees it falls back; carried past about 95 it folds forward. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the robot on its back between the rocks on its marks, arms along its trunk, legs straight; put the rocks back on their marks.
fidelity: Rigid links, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; hinges limp (damping 0.002 N m s/rad, no friction or spring), hard end stops. Sizes, masses and joint ranges are a 1:3 scale of a public mid-size humanoid model (lengths x 1/3, masses x 1/27); shapes are boxes, capsules and spheres; no waist joint; the hatch is a painted panel. The turf strip is drawn on the rigid pad. No forces or damage are simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm reached in over the robot's legs and the left arm came near, but neither moved it; it stayed on its back); demo: 1.0
